name: Iron Sage
summary: The Iron Sage is what iron-rich worked ground produces instead of ore: while a face is being cut it sits on the deposit and the seam runs clean, and when the cutting stops it sits there anyway, so every binding ground on the plains is somebody's working face. Holding the face therefore holds a thing that improves the ore, while owning the sage owns nothing - it follows the iron and not the deed, and has outlasted at least one proprietor.

attributes.drawn_by: worked iron ground rather than unworked deposit, so it only ever appears on somebody's claim
attributes.what_it_is_worth: a cleaner seam while the cutting continues, and nothing whatever after it stops
attributes.what_it_costs: the holder of the face is committed to the face - a sage that improves the ore is a reason to keep cutting a finite total
attributes.what_it_means_today: the only plains figure that is a liability without a working face, which is why it changes hands when a claim changes hands
attributes.held_by: nobody; it has outlived at least one proprietor

name: Storm Phoenix
summary: The Storm Phoenix binds open sky to a rising current and refuses everything else, which on a tier that writes elemental law nowhere at the bottom rung is a binding that never quite takes. It sits on a phoenix's ground because that ground is the closest the Mortal Plains come to a licensed elemental substrate, and it is weaker here than anywhere else in the setting for exactly that reason.

attributes.drawn_by: open sky plus a rising current, neither of which this tier can license
attributes.what_it_is_worth: the only elemental sight a mortal-tier holder can buy, and it is a partial one
attributes.what_it_costs: the holder of the ground has to keep the current rising, which on a tier with no temporal law written is an argument rather than a schedule
attributes.what_it_means_today: the setting's most instructive failure: a full-strength technique and no licensed substrate, standing next to each other
attributes.held_by: nobody in particular; the ground is held because the binding makes it worth holding

name: Void Serpent
summary: The Void Serpent binds to water that has just gone somewhere else, and it holds its ground on the flood line rather than the bank, so its presence is a statement about drainage and not about depth. On the plains that means it appears where the Widow Run has been and not where it is, which makes it the only figure on this tier that can be dated by its own ground. What it costs whoever holds the line is a river that has to keep misbehaving on schedule.

attributes.drawn_by: water that has just gone somewhere else, so the binding is always downstream of an event
attributes.what_it_is_worth: a ground that can be dated, which is worth more on a tier where nothing else can be surveyed
attributes.what_it_costs: the holder needs the river to keep moving its bed, which is the one thing the plains cannot arrange and can only read
attributes.what_it_means_today: the only reliably datable thing on the Mortal Plains, because its ground records an event rather than a season
attributes.held_by: whoever holds the flood line, which changes with the river

name: Iron Titan
summary: The Iron Titan is assembled out of the slag of a spent seam, which makes it the only figure in the setting made entirely of what a mine left behind. It stands on a heap that has not moved in forty years because nothing on this tier has the spatial law to shift it, so its body is also its ground and the two are the same object.

attributes.made_from: the slag of a worked-out seam, which is the only material on this tier that is free
attributes.what_it_is_worth: nothing as ore and everything as an obstacle; it is the largest single object the spoil guild has never moved
attributes.what_it_costs: the working face - a heap with a figure on it cannot be hauled, so the seam's floor is blocked for as long as it stands
attributes.what_it_means_today: the setting's clearest proof that exhaustion on a three-slot world is a permanent addition rather than a supply problem
attributes.held_by: nobody; it is not owned, it is an obstruction

name: Storm Phoenix
summary: The Storm Phoenix at the forge ground is not a bird that survived being burnt; it is a fire that was built to the shape of one out of the only fuel the plains produce, which is hot worked ground. It therefore needs open sky and a rising current to hold its shape, and this tier has neither licensed, so the most impressive object on the Mortal Plains is the setting's largest example of a technique running at full strength and producing nothing.

attributes.made_from: hot worked ground - the only fuel this tier produces and the only one that is free
attributes.what_it_is_worth: a demonstration rather than a creature; nothing it does can be repeated below the ley
attributes.what_it_costs: the weather - the shape only holds in an open sky with a rising current, and neither can be arranged on a tier with no temporal law
attributes.what_it_means_today: the setting's most expensive proof that an unwritten law removes a technique instead of weakening it
attributes.held_by: the forge ground, which is held because the sight is worth the ground

name: Void Leviathan
summary: The Void Leviathan was assembled from the deepest cold water on the only coastline that holds its shape, which is a coastline on the spirit tier and a fact the plains cannot produce: a tier with no spatial law cannot keep a shore in place. It therefore stands at a forge ground on ground borrowed from a higher tier's geography, which is the clearest sign in the setting that the Mortal Plains is a floor and not a world.

attributes.made_from: the deepest cold water on the one coastline that holds its shape, which is a spirit-tier fact
attributes.what_it_is_worth: a coastline's worth of standing water, imported into a tier that cannot keep a coast in place
attributes.what_it_costs: the shore - the figure only holds while the water it was built from stays where it was put
attributes.what_it_means_today: the setting's clearest demonstration that the bottom rung is a floor, not a world, and that its geography is being supplied from above
attributes.held_by: the forge ground, which holds a thing made of a place it does not have

name: Ironhide Bear
summary: The Ironhide Bear is the plains' great grazer and the only bear here whose hide is armour, and it ranges the herb belt it is defending, which means the belt has to be defended twice. Its hide is the only material on the mortal tier that stops a blade, and it grazes the only plant that grows here, so the tier's armour and the tier's medicine are the same animal and the same ground.

attributes.grazes: ecology.spirit_herb in geography.bitter_scrub, the only ground on the plains where the plant grows
attributes.what_it_is_worth: the only hide that stops a blade on this tier, and the reason the herb belt is defended rather than fenced
attributes.what_it_costs: the belt - one bear taken is a belt grazed harder, which is a medical shortage before it is a hunger
attributes.what_it_means_today: the tier's ecological anchor: taking it is taking the plains' armour and their medicine in one stroke
attributes.held_by: nothing; it is defended, and the defence is a habit rather than an office

name: Storm Hawk
summary: The Storm Hawk hunts the updraught off hot worked ground, so it follows the seams rather than the scrub and its range is a map of where anybody has been cutting. It is the only large predator on the plains that is not competing for the herb, which is why a hawk can be abundant while a bear is hunted out. What it costs the ground underneath is that every cutting makes an updraught, and an updraught is an invitation.

attributes.hunts: the updraught off hot worked ground, so its range is the exhausted seam and the flats rather than the herb belt
attributes.what_it_is_worth: a read on where work has happened, available from the air and to nobody who cannot fly
attributes.what_it_costs: the range - every cutting makes an updraught and every updraught is an invitation, so working the flats feeds the hawk
attributes.what_it_means_today: the only large predator here that is abundant, because it is not competing with the people for the only plant
attributes.held_by: nobody; it is a consequence of everyone else's labour

name: Venom Serpent
summary: The Venom Serpent lives in wet ground that only exists during the flood, so its range is measured in weeks a year and it is the only figure on the plains whose territory is a date rather than a place. That makes it the setting's most precisely dated animal and the least claimable: nobody can hold a serpent's ground, because the ground is a month. What it costs the households on the Widow Run is a medical shortage that arrives on a schedule nobody can move.

attributes.lives_in: wet ground that exists only during the flood, so the range is measured in weeks a year
attributes.what_it_is_worth: a date rather than a claim - the most precisely located animal on the plains and the least holdable
attributes.what_it_costs: the households on the run, who get a bite season they cannot reschedule and cannot fence against
attributes.what_it_means_today: the reason a settlement on the Widow Run is revocable once a generation, independently of the river
attributes.held_by: nobody; a serpent's ground is a month and a month is not a property

name: Blood Refining Guardian
summary: The Blood Refining Guardian holds the eighth gate on a ring wide and unbroken, because everything the practitioner has taken apart has to be reassembled on one site and a divided ground would let a body be returned in pieces. It is the only gate whose arena was widened rather than deepened, and the widening is the whole of its doctrine. What it costs is completeness: a reassembly that leaves anything out is not a lesser practitioner but a shorter-lived one.

attributes.why_this_ground: everything taken apart has to be reassembled on one site, so the ring was widened rather than cut
attributes.what_it_holds: a continuous piece of ground with no internal boundary, which is the only arena on the ring that can refuse to let a body be split
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: completeness - anything left out of the reassembly is gone for the rest of a hundred-year life
attributes.what_it_means_today: the last mortal gate, and the one whose ground was reshaped to make the rule enforceable rather than argued
attributes.staffed_by: visitors, since the tier licenses no humanoid

name: Bone Refining Guardian
summary: The Bone Refining Guardian holds the third gate in a pit cut into living stone, because the first closed centre a practitioner builds will resonate with any hollow it finds, and a hollow in unworked rock is the only thing on the ring quiet enough to close one in. It is the only figure on the Cairn Field that was dug rather than appointed, and the excavation is still visible as the reason the gate has no queue.

attributes.why_this_ground: the first closed centre wants a hard floor and no resonance, so the gate was cut into unworked rock rather than built on the surface
attributes.what_it_holds: a pit whose floor is the only resonance-free surface within a season's walk, and which is therefore worth more than any ore on the flats
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: years, and a measurable ringing that the lichen and the rock both keep after the practitioner leaves
attributes.what_it_means_today: the gate that proves the Iron Grief was a supply failure and not a ceiling - a core forms here, and forms only where somebody cut a hole
attributes.staffed_by: visitors, since the tier licenses no humanoid

name: Body of Divinity Guardian
summary: The Body of Divinity Guardian holds the penultimate gate on the deepest ground the top tier has, on the reasoning that an ancestor position has to be held where nothing above it is left to be summoned by. It is the only figure in the setting that has survived being cited, and it has been cited in three separate attempts to fill a vacant seat, each of which failed on the same ground. What it costs is continuation: nothing here can be inherited, only re-attempted.

attributes.why_this_ground: an ancestor position is held on the deepest ground the tier has, because everything above it is surplus
attributes.what_it_holds: the deepest ground on the shelf, and a position that cannot be inherited and can only be re-attempted
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: continuity - no result here passes to anybody
attributes.what_it_means_today: the figure three separate attempts to fill a vacant seat have cited and failed against
attributes.staffed_by: no standing staff; the three cited attempts were all visitors

name: Body of Heaven Guardian
summary: The Body of Heaven Guardian holds the gate where a completed frame is put out to bear something, and it stands on planted ground at the edge of the ley so the proof is a living one rather than a measurement. It is the only figure on the ring that grows anything, and the planting is the examination: a frame that cannot sustain what it puts out cannot pass. What it costs is the planting itself - two seasons of a terrace's yield surrendered to a test.

attributes.why_this_ground: a completed frame put out to bear something is proved on planted ground at the ley's edge
attributes.what_it_holds: the ring's only farm, where the candidate's frame is tested by whether what it puts out survives
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: two seasons of a terrace's yield, surrendered to a test whose result is biological
attributes.what_it_means_today: the only gate on any ring whose verdict arrives late and cannot be recalled
attributes.staffed_by: outsiders, because a candidate must be judged by a frame that is not itself a candidate

name: Body of Creation Guardian
summary: The Body of Creation Guardian holds the immortal band's opening gate against the ley beneath the ground rather than the sky above it, because the first immortal frame is earth-shaped and a frame proved from below is the only way to find out whether it will hold a weight the mortal tier could never cage. It is the first gate in the setting whose proof is downward, and the Terrace Ring's cut terraces exist because this figure needed a floor it could dig.

attributes.why_this_ground: the first immortal frame is earth-shaped, so the ley it is proved against is below rather than above
attributes.what_it_holds: the ring's cut terraces, dug downward so that a frame could be tested against the ley underneath it
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: perpetual upkeep - essence is the first resource priced by period rather than by weight
attributes.what_it_means_today: the gate that proved a body could carry a resource no mortal frame could hold, at the cost of a permanent settlement
attributes.staffed_by: outsiders, because a candidate must be judged by a frame that is not itself a candidate

name: Muscle Forging Guardian
summary: The first rung of the Body ladder, and the only gate on the Cairn Field held on ground chosen for flatness rather than for ore, because a frame has to be set before it can carry anything at all. It stands where nothing worth mining is, which on the Ironhead Flats is the only honest place a mortal could stand and the only ground here nobody has ever quarrelled over.

attributes.why_this_ground: a frame is set before it carries anything, so the ring was cut on flatness and not on ore
attributes.what_it_holds: the working face of the first gate, which nobody may reach before dawn because the ground is read at first light
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: nothing recoverably - the first gate's failure is a body that never closes a core, which is a hundred-year life spent ordinary
attributes.what_it_means_today: the only gate on the ring with no queue, because nobody stakes a decade of life on a rung that only proves the frame holds
attributes.staffed_by: visitors, since the tier licenses no humanoid

name: Body of Eternity Guardian
summary: The Body of Eternity Guardian holds the endurance gate on the one piece of ground in the immortal tier that nothing has ever broken, and it has held that ground long enough that the ring's own records treat its unbrokenness as the finding rather than the test. It is the only figure at this band that is best described as evidence: it does not judge, it demonstrates, and the demonstration has lasted longer than most of the claims made about it.

attributes.why_this_ground: an endurance test belongs on the one ground in the tier nothing has ever broken
attributes.what_it_holds: an unbroken terrace, which is a finding rather than a test - nothing has managed to break it and nothing has managed to leave
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: time at a clock five to fifty times slower, which is the only thing this gate can actually take
attributes.what_it_means_today: the ring's oldest continuous record, and the reason the terrace above it was never cut for stone
attributes.staffed_by: outsiders, because a candidate must be judged by a frame that is not itself a candidate

name: Iron Body Guardian
summary: The Iron Body Guardian stands on the heaviest ground the Mortal Plains has, because the ninth gate is the first refusal to break and a refusal is only credible on a floor that has already refused something. It is the last gate of the mortal band and the only one nobody has ever described as passable by a resident, which is a statistical fact rather than a policy.

attributes.why_this_ground: the first refusal to break is a structural test, so it is stood on the heaviest ground the tier has
attributes.what_it_holds: the mortal band's last gate, beyond which the plains have nothing to offer a practitioner
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: the belief that the ladder continues; crossing it is legal and terminal
attributes.what_it_means_today: the gate that turned a ceiling into a decision - after it, walking up to the Spirit Peaks was an economic choice rather than a spiritual one
attributes.staffed_by: visitors, since the tier licenses no humanoid

name: Body of Origin Guardian
summary: The Body of Origin Guardian holds the gate for a net of causes kept open, and it stands where the ley lines cross rather than on any one of them, because a network cannot be tested at a point. It is the only figure at this band that publishes what it is looking at, which the ring's other eight do not, and the publication is the reason its verdicts have never once been successfully disputed.

attributes.why_this_ground: a net of causes held open wants the crossing the ley lines make rather than any one of them
attributes.what_it_holds: the ring's only published gate, sited where the ley lines cross
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: particularity - a net held open cannot act on a single strand
attributes.what_it_means_today: the only verdicts on the ring that have never been successfully disputed, and the reason is that anybody may check the method
attributes.staffed_by: outsiders, because a candidate must be judged by a frame that is not itself a candidate

name: Body of Destruction Guardian
summary: The Body of Destruction Guardian holds its gate under open sky with nothing overhead, because a frame proved against what comes down needs to be able to see the whole of it. It is the only figure at this band that has ever refused a candidate on the grounds that the ground was too sheltered, which makes it the setting's one adversarial examiner rather than a gate. What it costs is shelter: every convenience the terrace ring offers is a subtraction from the test.

attributes.why_this_ground: a frame proved against what comes down wants open sky and nothing overhead
attributes.what_it_holds: the ring's only unsheltered ground, kept that way on purpose
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: shelter - every comfort the terrace ring offers is a subtraction from the test
attributes.what_it_means_today: the ring's only gate that has refused a candidate for being too well prepared
attributes.staffed_by: outsiders, because a candidate must be judged by a frame that is not itself a candidate

name: Body of Earth Guardian
summary: The Body of Earth Guardian holds its gate at the ring's edge, and the edge is the whole of the doctrine: command exercised at scale is measured from the outside of the terraces, so the figure stands where the ring it commands ends and issues authority backwards over ground it has never set foot inside. It is the only figure at this band that has ever held a territory, and the territory is the trial ring it is judging.

attributes.why_this_ground: command exercised at scale is measured from the ring's edges, so the ring commands the whole terrace
attributes.what_it_holds: the ring itself, as a territory, judged from outside its own boundary
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: proximity - nothing under this figure's command can be helped from where it stands
attributes.what_it_means_today: the setting's only territory held by a gate, which is why the council has never been able to say who owns the ring
attributes.staffed_by: outsiders, because a candidate must be judged by a frame that is not itself a candidate

name: Body of Immortality Guardian
summary: The Body of Immortality Guardian holds its gate on ground that is itself already unproven, on the reasoning that a claim nobody can check has to be held somewhere nobody else can check either. It is the ring's only gate whose site is deliberately doubtful, and the doubt is the practice. What it costs is verifiability: a pass here is a claim, and the ground cannot be used to support it. Meeting it today is being made to prove a thing on a site where proof has no purchase.

attributes.why_this_ground: a claim that cannot be checked is held on ground that is itself already unproven
attributes.what_it_holds: a terrace whose own survey has never agreed with itself, which makes it the only gate that cannot be used to support its own verdict
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: verifiability - a pass is a claim and the ground will not corroborate it
attributes.what_it_means_today: the ring's standing precedent for holding an unverifiable office, four realms before four such offices were written down
attributes.staffed_by: outsiders, because a candidate must be judged by a frame that is not itself a candidate

name: Marrow Cleansing Guardian
summary: The Marrow Cleansing Guardian is the first gate on the ring where something can simply be gone afterwards, and it is placed on the most heavily watched ground on the Cairn Field for that reason rather than for difficulty. It has never been found absent from its ground, which is the only continuity any of the nine can point to, and every account of the gate agrees on that fact and disagrees on everything else.

attributes.why_this_ground: what can be lost is first held here, so the ground is watched and never left unguarded
attributes.what_it_holds: the only gate whose occupant has never been recorded missing, which makes it the ring's oldest continuous witness
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: marrow, permanently; a body that fails here is shorter-lived and cannot be repaired on this tier
attributes.what_it_means_today: the gate that changed the arithmetic - before it, failure was practice; after it, failure was a permanent subtraction
attributes.staffed_by: visitors, since the tier licenses no humanoid

name: Body of Unity Guardian
summary: The Body of Unity Guardian holds its gate where several laws are written at once, which on this tier happens only because ten slots over six groups leaves duplicate imprints and a duplicate has to be imitated by something. It is the only figure at this band that is not testing one frame against one law, and it is the gate that the four unfillable immortal seats are quietly made to resemble.

attributes.why_this_ground: unity attempted where several laws are written at once, which only the duplicate imprints permit
attributes.what_it_holds: the one ground on the ring where four duplicate imprints have to be imitated by a body rather than argued about above it
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: distinction - afterwards there is no telling which of the several things is responsible for anything
attributes.what_it_means_today: the ring's last gate before the transcendent floor, and the setting's clearest working model of an unfillable seat
attributes.staffed_by: outsiders, because a candidate must be judged by a frame that is not itself a candidate

name: Body of the Dao Guardian
summary: The Body of the Dao Guardian holds the last rung of the Body ladder on ground that is itself a broken law and has not finished curing, and it is the setting's clearest case of a test that is hostile to the thing being tested. The last frame a Body practitioner attempts is attempted on a fracture, and the figure standing at the fracture is not a gatekeeper so much as the reason the attempt is dangerous. Every account of it is an account of damage.

attributes.why_this_ground: the last frame is attempted on ground that is itself a broken law and is still curing
attributes.what_it_holds: a fracture in the substrate, and the last gate the Body ladder has
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: the ladder - there is no rung above this one for a Body practitioner to arrive at
attributes.what_it_means_today: the setting's clearest case of a test hostile to the thing tested, and the end of the Body road rather than a rung on it
attributes.staffed_by: no standing staff; every account of this gate describes damage

name: Skin Tempering Guardian
summary: The Skin Tempering Guardian holds the second gate on ground that is deliberately open and flooded, because the first charge a body carries has to be held somewhere that will not move and standing water is the only thing on the plains that demonstrates that. It has therefore spent four decades standing in a flood line on a tier whose only river moves its bed once a generation, and it is the only figure on the ring whose ground is unreliable by design.

attributes.why_this_ground: the first charge must be held somewhere that cannot move, and a flood line is the plains' only proof of stillness
attributes.what_it_holds: a flood line that relocates when the Widow Run turns over, so the gate has to be re-read every season
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: a season's work at a time, for as long as the ground stays where it was last read
attributes.what_it_means_today: the cheapest gate to enter and the most expensive to be wrong at, because the water decides the calendar and nobody argues with the Widow Run
attributes.staffed_by: visitors, since the tier licenses no humanoid

name: Body of Chaos Guardian
summary: The Body of Chaos Guardian holds the gate where the departure has no return step, and it stands with every exit of its ground facing outward, which is not a design decision so much as a refusal: the arena will not let anybody turn back into it once the pass has begun. It is the only figure on the spirit ring that has turned the architecture of a trial into its verdict.

attributes.why_this_ground: a departure with no return step, and so every exit of the ground faces outward
attributes.what_it_holds: the spirit band's last gate, whose exits are one-directional by construction
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: the tier - upkeep rises about fortyfold per tier and a completed body has to be paid for at the next one
attributes.what_it_means_today: the gate that is also a border, which is why it is scheduled at a tide and staffed by whoever can read an assay
attributes.staffed_by: competitors, because a gate on the quarry floor has to be staffed by whoever can read the assay

name: Silver Body Guardian
summary: The Silver Body Guardian holds the spirit band's second gate on the quarry floor rather than the ridge above it, because the first reservoir fills fastest where the ambient qi is already dense and density is measured in cut lengths per unit of ground worked. It stands on the one institution in the setting that measures a world instead of praising it, which makes it the most accurately sited figure here and the least sentimental.

attributes.why_this_ground: the first reservoir fills fastest where ambient qi is densest, so it is sited on the worked face itself
attributes.what_it_holds: the quarry floor's own density reading, which is the only verifiable figure in the spirit tier
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: cut lengths of spirit stone, priced before the sale and published after it
attributes.what_it_means_today: the gate that turned a hole into evidence - the standing figure on the floor is standing on the Density Ceiling's measurement
attributes.staffed_by: competitors, because a gate on the quarry floor has to be staffed by whoever can read the assay

name: Body of Dao Guardian
summary: The Body of Dao Guardian holds the rung at which a practitioner first carries a place, and the ground is chosen as the one they intend to carry, which makes it the only gate on any ring where the arena is selected by the person being judged. Every crossing has therefore left a patch of the Spirit Peaks that a practitioner's frame will not tolerate leaving, and those patches are the setting's clearest inventory of who has held ground and let it go. What it costs is mobility.

attributes.why_this_ground: the first time a practitioner carries a place, the ground chosen is the one they intend to carry
attributes.what_it_holds: a self-selected arena, which makes it the only gate on any ring that the candidate chooses
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: mobility - a frame that carries a place will not tolerate being far from it, and the patch is left behind
attributes.what_it_means_today: the gate that produced the setting's inventory of held-and-abandoned ground
attributes.staffed_by: competitors, because a gate on the quarry floor has to be staffed by whoever can read the assay

name: Diamond Body Guardian
summary: The Diamond Body Guardian holds the gate where what a practitioner projects has to land on something real, and it stands against a wall for that reason: a projection with nothing behind it is an assertion, and this ring does not certify assertions. It is the only figure here that judges appearance rather than capacity, and the distinction is the reason its verdicts are the ones practitioners argue about.

attributes.why_this_ground: what is projected has to land on something real, so the site needs a wall to be seen against
attributes.what_it_holds: the only wall on the spirit ring, built as a testing surface rather than as a boundary
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: conviction - a manifestation that reads well and lands badly is failed here while a plain one that lands passes
attributes.what_it_means_today: the gate that made technique records comparable, because from here a claim could be checked against a surface
attributes.staffed_by: competitors, because a gate on the quarry floor has to be staffed by whoever can read the assay

name: Jade Body Guardian
summary: The Jade Body Guardian holds the gate for an interior built inside a practitioner, and it stands in enclosing stone with the wind stopped, because a room that has to survive its own inhabitant cannot be built on open ground. It is the only figure on the spirit band's ring that has been constructed rather than found, and the construction is why the ring's schedule is built around it.

attributes.why_this_ground: an interior built inside a practitioner wants enclosing stone and no wind
attributes.what_it_holds: the only constructed arena on the spirit ring, and the only one with a roof
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: the right to leave, permanently, once the interior is finished
attributes.what_it_means_today: the ring's only building, which is why the ring's calendar is published around a roof rather than a mark on the ground
attributes.staffed_by: competitors, because a gate on the quarry floor has to be staffed by whoever can read the assay

name: Gold Body Guardian
summary: The Gold Body Guardian holds the gate that makes a reservoir wide enough to hold a failure, and it is sited on a quarry floor for the unglamorous reason that a floor can take the weight of a sea that has just gone wrong. Nobody who has crossed it has described the gate afterwards; the accounts agree only that the ground had to be wide and had to be hard.

attributes.why_this_ground: a reservoir wide enough to hold a failure belongs on a quarry floor and not on a ridge
attributes.what_it_holds: the only ground on the ring wide enough to absorb a sea that has failed to form
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: everything in the reservoir at once, uncontained, and there is no later gate on this ladder that returns it
attributes.what_it_means_today: the gate with no surviving description, which makes it the setting's most reliable witness and its least legible one
attributes.staffed_by: competitors, because a gate on the quarry floor has to be staffed by whoever can read the assay

name: Adamant Body Guardian
summary: The Adamant Body Guardian holds the gate for a cut that must complete, and it stands on one unbroken line of force with nothing standing on it, because an interrupted severing is not a partial result but a wound. It is the only figure on the spirit ring whose ground has been kept deliberately empty for four decades of use, and the emptiness is the whole of its practice.

attributes.why_this_ground: a cut that must complete needs one unbroken line of force and no interruption
attributes.what_it_holds: a length of ground kept clear of everything for four decades, including the equipment that would have helped
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: the ability to stop once started; the ground sets the time and does not extend it
attributes.what_it_means_today: the gate that made self-inflicted wound a known quantity rather than a surprise
attributes.staffed_by: competitors, because a gate on the quarry floor has to be staffed by whoever can read the assay

name: Body of Void Guardian
summary: The Body of Void Guardian holds the rung where authority is exercised over an empty space, and it stands on the emptiest ground the spirit tier has, which is a quarry floor after a cut rather than before one. The choice is the argument: command that needs a subject has nothing to test, so the ground is cleared and the figure is left holding authority over nothing at all. What it costs is any proof of rule, because nothing on an empty floor ever obeys anything.

attributes.why_this_ground: authority over a hollow space is tested on the emptiest ground the tier has
attributes.what_it_holds: a cleared floor after a cut, holding authority over nothing that has ever obeyed it
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: proof - nothing on an empty floor complies, so a pass here is a claim with no witness
attributes.what_it_means_today: the gate that predicted the immortal tier's four unfillable seats, four realms before anybody wrote them down
attributes.staffed_by: competitors, because a gate on the quarry floor has to be staffed by whoever can read the assay

name: Tendon Strengthening Guardian
summary: The Tendon Strengthening Guardian holds the fifth gate in the deepest cut on the Cairn Field, with every approach back out of it sealed, because the change it certifies cannot be taken back half way and a practitioner who turns around mid-pass is the one failure the ring cannot treat as practice. It is the only gate that physically refuses a retreat, and it has done so since before the Wound Run changed its bed and took the return path with it.

attributes.why_this_ground: a change that cannot be undone partway through needs depth and no way out
attributes.what_it_holds: the only gate on the ring with no approach a practitioner may walk back up, which is why the return path was sealed rather than left steep
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: the right to reverse the attempt, and with it the option of a shorter life with an intact frame
attributes.what_it_means_today: the gate that made the rest of the ladder a decision rather than a curriculum
attributes.staffed_by: visitors, since the tier licenses no humanoid

name: Body of Laws Guardian
summary: The Body of Laws Guardian holds the gate for several things held as one, and it occupies a whole section of the ring rather than a point on it, because unity attempted on a small patch is just a crowd. It is the only figure on the spirit band whose footprint is measured in acres and whose verdicts are read off the footprint rather than off the attempt.

attributes.why_this_ground: several things held as one wants a whole section of ground rather than a point on it
attributes.what_it_holds: the largest single footprint on any ring in the setting, kept as one surface with no dividing marks
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: separability - after a pass, one part of the frame cannot be worked on alone
attributes.what_it_means_today: the gate that turned the Body ladder's last mortal rung into a question about what a person is
attributes.staffed_by: competitors, because a gate on the quarry floor has to be staffed by whoever can read the assay

name: Body of Humanity Guardian
summary: The Body of Humanity Guardian holds the first gate on the Fragmentshelf, where the ground is a broken law, and it exists because fifteen imprints over three layers need a container larger than the Body ladder's arithmetic can describe. It is the only figure in the setting that has never been described by a resident of any tier below the top one, and every account of it agrees that it reads rather than strikes.

attributes.why_this_ground: the first frame that can hold the top tier's spatial reading needs a container this large
attributes.what_it_holds: the Fragmentshelf itself, where the substrate is broken law and is still curing
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: scale - three attempts have ever been possible on this shelf and fewer have ever been survived
attributes.what_it_means_today: the top rung the Body ladder can reach before it has to become something else
attributes.staffed_by: no standing staff; the three attempts were all visitors

name: Copper Body Guardian
summary: The Copper Body Guardian does not test the practitioner so much as apply the plains' own law pressure deliberately, and it stands where that pressure already runs near its ceiling so nobody has to import it. Three law slots on a hundred-year body is the whole of what a mortal world does to a person, and this is the gate that makes the world do it on purpose.

attributes.why_this_ground: the crossing applies the world's own law pressure deliberately, so it is sited where that pressure already runs near its ceiling
attributes.what_it_holds: the ceiling of what three written law groups do to a mortal body, applied on purpose rather than endured
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: years off the far end of a hundred-year life, which on this tier is the only currency a gate can charge
attributes.what_it_means_today: the gate that made the ladder legible - after it, everybody knew the tier had a ceiling and that the ceiling was a law
attributes.staffed_by: visitors, since the tier licenses no humanoid

name: Body of Transcendence Guardian
summary: The Body of Transcendence Guardian holds its gate where the ley thins out, on the principle that a frame which has stopped depending on the frame should be tested where there is least left to lean on. It is the only figure on the ring that has moved its own ground, having been sited elsewhere and transferred, and the transfer is the only recorded instance of a gate changing its own answer.

attributes.why_this_ground: the frame that stops depending on the frame is tested where the ley thins out
attributes.what_it_holds: the thinnest ground on the ring, and the only gate that has been transferred rather than sited
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: inheritance - nothing learned here can be passed to somebody standing on thick ground
attributes.what_it_means_today: the only recorded instance of a gate changing its own verdict, and the only reform the Terrace Ring has ever had
attributes.staffed_by: outsiders, because a candidate must be judged by a frame that is not itself a candidate

name: Organ Tempering Guardian
summary: The Organ Tempering Guardian holds the seventh gate on ground chosen for the void underneath it rather than the stone above it, because the hollowing a practitioner attempts has to make room before anything can be put in the room. It is sited over a cavity in the flats and it charges for the hollowing, which is the only gate on the ring whose cost falls on a resource rather than on a body.

attributes.why_this_ground: the hollowing makes room, so the ground was chosen for the void beneath it and not the stone above
attributes.what_it_holds: a cavity in the flats that a practitioner is charged against before anything is attempted
attributes.what_it_costs_the_practitioner: material, not years - the gate is the only one on the ring that prices its ground
attributes.what_it_means_today: the gate that proved the plains could be invoiced, and every gate fee after it is a descendant of that habit
attributes.staffed_by: visitors, since the tier licenses no humanoid

name: Iron Sage
summary: The Iron Sage at the archive keeps whatever is written down on iron-rich worked ground, which on the plains means the only records that have ever survived, because iron outlasts the paper and the paper outlasts the hand. It holds the burnt lists and the assay notes and nothing else: a Sage that held anything else would be holding a claim, and the settlement's whole position is that it holds records.

attributes.holds: assay notes and the burnt lists, and refuses anything that could be read as a claim
attributes.what_it_is_worth: the only records on this tier that survive a decade, because the medium is the tier's most durable material
attributes.what_it_costs: ore - every sheet is cut from the same iron as every tool, so the record is bought out of the resource the tier has least of
attributes.what_it_means_today: the plains' memory is real and it is finite, and every page spent on the past is a page not spent on a working face
attributes.held_by: the settlement on the face, which funds it and cannot audit it

name: Storm Phoenix
summary: The Storm Phoenix at the archive keeps the records that were made in weather, and on the Mortal Plains weather is the only event that recurs on a cycle anybody can rely on - temporal law is written here at 0.5-2.0 while qi sits on the floor, so the flood is a clock and nothing else is. What it therefore holds is a chronology rather than a ledger, and it is the reason the plains have a sequence at all.

attributes.holds: a chronology rather than a ledger - events in the order the weather put them
attributes.what_it_is_worth: the only dated sequence on this tier, because a flood is the only recurring event here with an interval
attributes.what_it_costs: accuracy - a record made in weather is a record made by somebody who was in it
attributes.what_it_means_today: the plains' sense of when things happened, which is a chronology and not an account
attributes.held_by: the ring, which needs a calendar more than it needs a ledger

name: Void Serpent
summary: The Void Serpent at the archive keeps the records of things that are absent, which is the only category the plains can supply honestly: a settlement that moves is a settlement that has to be un-recorded, and a river that relocates takes its names with it. It is therefore the archive the setting's missing persons are legible in, and every gap in it has a shape rather than being an oversight.

attributes.holds: records of what is gone - moved settlements, changed beds, and the names nobody is claiming
attributes.what_it_is_worth: the only place on this tier where an absence is a record rather than a failure
attributes.what_it_costs: standing - a record of what is gone is not a claim on anything and therefore cannot be made to owe
attributes.what_it_means_today: the plains' missing persons are legible here, and every gap has a shape rather than being an oversight
attributes.held_by: nobody claims it, which is the condition of it holding anything at all

name: Iron Monarch
summary: The Iron Monarch holds the only worked ground on the Mortal Plains that has a wall on it, which is the last standing face of a seam that stopped paying forty years ago, and its claim is therefore a claim to a ruin. It is not a crown: the seat it occupies was made by a building nobody else could hold, and the standing behind it is a claim about who keeps the face rather than a measurement of anything.

attributes.seat: the last standing face of the exhausted seam, the only worked ground on the plains with a wall
attributes.what_it_is_worth: a claim on a wall, which is the setting's cheapest form of authority and the only one available at this rung
attributes.what_it_costs: the heap - the wall stands on spoil nobody has cleared, and clearing it would dissolve the ground the claim rests on
attributes.what_it_means_today: a seat whose entire justification is that the ground under it is worthless to anybody who wants ore
attributes.held_by: whoever keeps the face, and the keeping is the office

name: Storm Sovereign
summary: The Storm Sovereign holds open ground at the crest of the Cairn Field, which is the only weather cycle the plains have and which is not a season and does not keep to one. It is therefore the setting's only throne that is appointed by weather, and the appointment cannot be contested because there is no calendar here that could state when the crest was wrong.

attributes.seat: open ground at the crest of the Cairn Field, on the plains' only weather cycle
attributes.what_it_is_worth: an uncontestable appointment, because no calendar exists here that could state the crest was wrong
attributes.what_it_costs: the ring - the sovereign occupies the gathering ground, so the most powerful figure at this rung is also the one standing in the crowd
attributes.what_it_means_today: the only throne in the setting whose tenure is set by something nobody has bothered to measure
attributes.held_by: the crest, which arrives and does not explain itself

name: Void Emperor
summary: The Void Emperor holds a seat on the Tier Stair, and it is on the stair rather than beside it because the stair is the only road in the setting whose position can be described the same way twice. Its claim is therefore to a measurement rather than to a territory, and a measurement cannot be inherited because a new one has to be taken.

attributes.seat: the Tier Stair, the only road in the setting whose position can be described the same way twice
attributes.what_it_is_worth: a claim to a measurement, which cannot be inherited because a new one has to be taken
attributes.what_it_costs: permanence - the seat survives only as long as somebody keeps measuring the stair
attributes.what_it_means_today: the only seat in the setting whose territory is a road, and the only one everybody on it is leaving
attributes.held_by: whoever last took the reading

name: Iron Sage Adept Lesser
summary: The Iron Sage Adept is a practitioner who has learned to read a binding rather than to hold one, and it stands on the same worked ground as the Iron Sage because that is the only place the lesson can be learned. It is called lesser because it is smaller, not because it is weaker: an adept that has read a hundred working faces knows which of them is still being cut, which is the only question the plains' economy turns on.

attributes.what_it_knows: which working faces are still being cut, which is the only question the plains' economy turns on
attributes.what_it_costs: proximity - being right about a claim is not the same as being permitted to keep it
attributes.what_it_means_today: the only person on the plains who can tell a live face from a dead one without being told
attributes.held_by: nobody; the lesson is public and the ground is not

name: Iron Sage Disciple Lesser
summary: The Iron Sage Disciple is what happens when somebody decides the archive is worth a career: it works the iron sheets, learns the assay, and becomes the first person able to say how much of a record survives a decade. It is lesser because it files rather than keeps, and the distinction is the whole of the settlement's position - a Sage holds records, a Disciple maintains them, and only one of the two is an office.

attributes.what_it_does: maintains the archive's iron sheets and learns the assay
attributes.what_it_costs: finiteness - every sheet is ore and the ore is not coming, so the work is a stock taking with an end
attributes.what_it_means_today: the office below the archive, and the only one on the plains that will not exist in a generation
attributes.held_by: the archive, which can be argued with and cannot be replaced

name: Iron Titan Slag Lesser
summary: The Iron Titan Slag is a piece of the forty-year heap that has taken a shape, and it is smaller than the titan because the heap is not homogeneous and the pieces that cohere first are the ones nearest the ore that was there. It sheds continuously and cannot be moved without breaking, so it is the setting's clearest example of a thing that is stable only where it lies. What it costs is permanence of nobody's choosing: the heap has not moved in forty years and neither has this.

attributes.what_it_is: a cohered piece of the heap, nearest the ore that was there
attributes.what_it_costs: nothing, deliberately - it cannot be moved without breaking, which makes it the heap's most cooperative obstruction
attributes.what_it_means_today: the spoil guild's daily problem in a single object, and the reason the tally has four decades of gaps in it
attributes.held_by: nobody; it is an obstruction that sheds

name: Ironhide Bear Cub Lesser
summary: The Ironhide Bear Cub is born without armour and grows it, which makes it the only figure in the setting whose value is a future one rather than a present one. Its hide is useless for forty years, so the tier's best armour is a thing that has to be fed and defended through a period in which it cannot pay back the ground it eats. What it costs is herb from the belt, taken before it can graze, so every cub on the plains is a claim on the only medicine in the world.

attributes.what_it_is_worth: nothing yet - the hide is useless for forty years, so the cub is a cost before it is an asset
attributes.what_it_costs: herb taken out of the belt before it can graze, which makes every cub a claim on the world's only medicine
attributes.what_it_means_today: the plains' future stock, and the reason nobody who takes one is trusted twice
attributes.held_by: nobody; the herd defends it and the belt feeds it

name: Storm Hawk Hatchling Lesser
summary: The Storm Hawk Hatchling cannot hunt, which on this tier means it cannot feed, because the only thing worth hunting is the updraught off hot worked ground and a hatchling cannot be carried there. It is therefore raised on whatever the adults bring down, which makes the plains' only abundant predator the one whose young are a permanent drain on the ones that work. What it costs the range is a season per clutch.

attributes.what_it_is_worth: nothing yet - it cannot hunt, and the only thing worth hunting here is a working updraught
attributes.what_it_costs: a season per clutch, carried by the adults that can work
attributes.what_it_means_today: the reason the plains' most abundant predator has never become a problem, and never become a resource either
attributes.held_by: the range, which feeds it whether or not anybody notices

name: Storm Phoenix Ember Lesser
summary: The Storm Phoenix Ember is the part of a forge fire that has separated from the body it was built to and has not gone out, which on this tier is possible precisely because elemental law is unwritten here and nothing licenses the fire to finish what it started. It is therefore the setting's only example of a technique that is losing its shape with nothing to stop it, and it has been losing it for forty years without ever burning out.

attributes.what_it_is: a fire that separated from the forge figure it was built into and has not gone out
attributes.what_it_costs: containment - nothing at this tier licenses it to finish what it started, so it cannot be put out
attributes.what_it_means_today: the setting's only demonstration that a missing law is a licence absent rather than a force absent
attributes.held_by: nobody; it has been losing its shape for forty years without anyone able to stop it

name: Storm Phoenix Fledgling Lesser
summary: The Storm Phoenix Fledgling is a binding that has not yet decided what it is bound to, and it holds a binding ground on the Mortal Plains by sitting on it, which means a practitioner has to decide whether to wait for the fledgling or to walk to another face entirely. It is lesser than the full binding in the only way that matters here: it has not yet started running the seam clean, so nothing on the plains has a price for it yet.

attributes.what_it_is_worth: nothing yet - it has not begun running the seam clean, so nothing on the plains has a price for it
attributes.what_it_costs: time - the working face will be cut past it or it will settle, and neither outcome is the holder's choice
attributes.what_it_means_today: the ground's next thousand loads have no owner yet, which is the only speculation on the plains worth making
attributes.held_by: the face, which is still being cut

name: Venom Serpent Fledgling Lesser
summary: The Venom Serpent Fledgling is the only large predator on the plains whose territory is four weeks wide and whose young cannot leave it, so it is raised in the one part of the Widow Run that a household has already given up. What it costs is the household: a settlement on the run keeps a stock of spirit herb precisely because of this figure, and the stock is the reason the settlement stays.

attributes.what_it_is_worth: a month of territory and a stock of medicine it causes to be kept
attributes.what_it_costs: the household - a settlement keeps a herb stock precisely because of this figure
attributes.what_it_means_today: the reason a hundred-year body on the Widow Run pays a yearly tax in medicine rather than in money
attributes.held_by: nobody; it is the reason a household stays

name: Void Leviathan Spawn Lesser
summary: The Void Leviathan Spawn is made from the same imported cold water as its parent and therefore cannot be made anywhere on the Mortal Plains, which means it was assembled somewhere else and brought down the Tier Stair. It is the setting's clearest evidence that goods move between tiers and residents do not: a thing built out of a spirit-tier coastline is standing on a three-slot world, and nothing about the plains could have produced it. What it costs is the road.

attributes.made_from: the same spirit-tier cold water as its parent, so it had to be built off the plains and brought down
attributes.what_it_costs: the road - a haulage route has to be kept clear and the animal has to be kept cold
attributes.what_it_means_today: the clearest proof in the setting that goods cross tiers and residents do not
attributes.held_by: nobody; it is a cargo that arrived

name: Void Serpent Venomling Lesser
summary: The Void Serpent Venomling is small enough to be carried and old enough to be responsible for something, which on the Mortal Plains is an unusual combination and the reason it holds a flood line at all. It binds to water that has just gone somewhere else, so a venomling on this ground is a small dated thing keeping a large dated record.

attributes.what_it_is_worth: a small dated thing holding a large dated record of where the water has gone
attributes.what_it_costs: handling - it has to be carried, and the plains' only carts belong to a guild
attributes.what_it_means_today: the setting's most portable record of a river's behaviour, and therefore the most valuable thing on the flood line
attributes.held_by: whoever is holding it, which changes with the flood

name: Aether Guardian Lesser
summary: The Aether Guardian posted to the Aether Domain is one of the first figures in the setting to stand on ground where an elemental technique actually does something, and it is lesser than the working elemental because it is a person and not a licensed form. Its whole function is to be on the one ground where fire and tide can be used so that somebody can compare it with the two dead grounds on the lower tiers.

attributes.what_it_is_worth: the control condition - a place where the same technique works so the two dead grounds can be compared against it
attributes.what_it_costs: home - every measurement it takes is worthless as a demonstration of anything below the ley
attributes.what_it_means_today: the setting's first controlled experiment, and it is standing at the control
attributes.held_by: the domain, which is worked ground and therefore held the way a resource is held

name: Ember Guardian Lesser
summary: The Ember Guardian is posted to the Ember Domain on the Mortal Plains, which is a dead elemental ground: elemental law is unspent there, so fire and tide run at full strength and produce nothing. Its entire function is to stand on a place where the technique fails and be legible evidence of it, and it has been doing that for long enough that the post has outlived every rotation.

attributes.what_it_is_worth: the proof that an unwritten law removes a technique rather than weakening it
attributes.what_it_costs: the practice - nothing a person at this tier can do with an elemental technique can be tested anywhere else on the plains
attributes.what_it_means_today: the setting's most expensive piece of negative evidence, and the post has outlived every rotation
attributes.held_by: the post, which nobody wants and nobody revokes

name: Gale Guardian Lesser
summary: The Gale Guardian stands at the Gale Domain on the Immortal Court, where elemental law is written and the weather is a licensed thing rather than an accident, and its work is turning a licensed storm into a calendar. It is lesser than the storm it governs because a person cannot set the Tidemark; what the delegate does is read it early and tell the shipping.

attributes.what_it_is_worth: a reading - it turns a licensed storm into a date and tells the shipping
attributes.what_it_costs: attribution - whoever is told the date sets it for everybody, including people who have never heard of the delegate
attributes.what_it_means_today: the setting's only authority that is obeyed without being named
attributes.held_by: the domain, which is worked ground on the court's upper terrace

name: Iron Monarch Lesser
summary: The Iron Monarch posted to the Iron Monarch's seat is not the seat and does not pretend to be: it stands on the spent seam's last standing face and reads the ground for whoever is holding the wall, which is a job rather than a throne. Its authority is entirely borrowed from the seat it stands beside, and the borrowing is visible to anybody who walks the heap.

attributes.what_it_is_worth: a reading - it reports the ground for whoever holds the wall and has no authority of its own
attributes.what_it_costs: the pretence - its authority is borrowed from the seat beside it and the borrowing is visible from the heap
attributes.what_it_means_today: the setting's clearest illustration of the gap between a claim and a crown, standing on waste
attributes.held_by: the seat, which lends standing and takes the ground

name: Storm Phoenix Lesser
summary: The Storm Phoenix posted to the Storm Phoenix Archive keeps the chronology that the archive's fire cannot keep for itself, because a figure whose element is unlicensed on this tier has no way to hold a record across a flood. It reads the sequence of events off the water and writes it on iron, and the writing is the reason the plains have a dated past at all. What it costs is the difference between a reading and an account: it can say what happened and not what it meant.

attributes.what_it_is_worth: a sequence - what happened and in what order, never what it meant
attributes.what_it_costs: the difference between a reading and an account, which is the difference between a record and a history
attributes.what_it_means_today: the reason the plains have a dated past, kept by something that was in the weather
attributes.held_by: the archive, which can be argued with and cannot be replaced
